status_summary: H.R. 10477, the Small Business Audit Correction Act of 2026 (Rep. Hill), was introduced on 2026-09-17 and referred to House Financial Services; S. 5454 (Sen. Cotton) was introduced on 2026-09-22 and referred to Senate Banking, and BILLSTATUS shows no later action on either. Section 2 of the House bill would amend section 110 of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act (15 U.S.C. 7220) to exclude privately held, non-carrying broker-dealers in good standing from the PCAOB-registered firm definitions and would direct the SEC to amend Rule 17a-5 so such firms can meet the annual audit duty with a GAAS audit within 180 days of the effective date. That is the audit exemption the Mandate describes, but it is a bill only, and the text does not mention peer-to-peer lending or Regulation CF. A Federal Register search of SEC documents since 2025-01-20 on broker-dealer audit and Rule 17a-5 returned no related proposed or final rule.

timeline.event: H.R. 10477 was introduced to exempt privately held, non-carrying broker-dealers from the PCAOB audit requirement and was referred to the House Financial Services Committee.
S. 5454, a related Senate bill also titled the Small Business Audit Correction Act of 2026 (Sen. Cotton), was introduced and referred to the Senate Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.
